* Experience writing tests to verify functionality and establishing monitoring systems to ensure code stability.
* Experience building APIs, service integrations, or automated workflows that connect multiple systems in production environments.

* Familiarity with source control, CI/CD, and automated testing practices for delivering reliable software.

* Background in mentoring new team members and contributing to engineering culture.

* Demonstrated ability to exercise sound judgment on engineering trade\-offs for complex systems.

The backbone of any technology org is its infrastructure, come join the team giving that skeleton superhuman abilities. The Infrastructure team at Mercury is an enablement lever for the rest of the business, building scaleable, secure and maintainable foundations for the rest of the org to build on top of.
   

  

 Infrastructure is currently building out more platform features to make it easier for agents and humans to deploy code. This means security by default, observable by default and easy to use and operate. We do all this while not compromising on speed, and ship to prod all day, every day, which is a testament to the strong foundations this team has built.
   

  

 We are looking for an engineer to join our team to help build out the “platform” even further! We maintain everything from networking to container orchestration, and work with product teams to enable any AWS needs they have. We want someone who is passionate about building maintainable systems, is obsessed with quality and making sure the sharp edges are filed off, and is extremely helpful when diving into problems with our product counterparts.
   

  

 This is a role for someone who likes going deep, shipping often, and leaving systems better than they found them. Someone who cares about quality without turning quality into bureaucracy. Someone who is just as happy debugging a strange Linux problem as they are helping a product engineer understand why their service behaves differently in production.
   

  

**Some of the technology you’ll work with**
 Our infrastructure is built primarily on AWS, including systems like EC2, RDS, OpenSearch, ECS, and EKS. We like to use the right tool for the job and bias towards cloud native open source tooling
   

  

 We use Terraform extensively to manage infrastructure as code, GitHub and GitHub Actions for version control and delivery, and Prometheus, Grafana, OpenSearch, and OpenTelemetry to understand what is happening in production.
   

  

 We’re also increasingly building
 **agentic infrastructure** 
 : systems that let AI agents safely interact with our infrastructure, and frameworks that give both agents and the humans operating them the right guardrails.
   

  

 You do not need to arrive knowing every tool we use. We care more about strong fundamentals, curiosity, and the ability to go deep.
   

  

 As we gear up for the next stages of Mercury's growth, you will:
   

  

* Build our “Infrastructure Platform” to support the growing needs of the Engineering Organization
* Focus on building a platform that is AI friendly while still usable for engineers. We want our users to be humans and Agents
* Deliver key infrastructure projects, break\-down complex initiatives, and define our infrastructure strategy through detailed RFCs and technical specifications


 Must haves:
   

  

* You have 2\+ years of experience with AWS
* You have a keen interest in cloud native open source technologies, and feel comfortable contributing code upstream to these technologies
* Strong knowledge of low\-level operating system foundations (linux, file systems, containers, etc)
* You have demonstrated ability in technical writing, with at least 2 years of experience creating detailed technical documentation, RFCs, and tech specs that clearly communicate complex ideas


 The ideal candidate should:
   

  

* Be used to operating in regulated environments such as HITRUST or SOC2, ensuring compliance and security
* Have 2\+ years of experience working in massive terraform environments, with many engineers contributing code in a scalable way
* Have 2\+ years of experience writing code. We are building an Infrastructure Platform from scratch and there is plenty of code to write to support that
* Be extremely willing to learn and dive into hard problems! We have many to solve!


 The Infrastructure team sits in an interesting place at Mercury: close enough to production that the details matter, and broad enough that a good abstraction can make hundreds of engineers faster.
   

  

 There is a lot left to build.
   

  

 If you like infrastructure that is secure by default, observable by default, pleasant to use, and designed for people who want to ship, we’d love to hear from you.
   

  

 If this role interests you, we invite you to explore our public demo at demo.mercury.com.

SOFTWARE ENGINEER, ENTERPRISE AI PLATFORM




🎨 ABOUT OPENART

OpenArt is an AI storytelling and visual creation platform used by millions of creators worldwide. We're building the next generation of creative tools powered by cutting-edge AI — enabling anyone to create videos, visuals, characters, and stories with unprecedented speed and imagination.

We believe the future of creativity is AI-native, and we're shaping that future.




🚀 WHY JOIN OPENART

 - Brand-new function, real mandate — enterprise and team customers are one of our biggest growth levers, and most of the infrastructure behind them hasn't been built yet. You'll be in on the ground floor.

 - Small team, massive surface area — engineers own real systems end to end, not slices.

 - Real scale, real stakes — OpenArt serves millions of creators, and enterprise deals will close (or not) on what you ship.

 - Founder-led engineering culture — both founders are technical and deeply involved in product and architecture.

 - AI-native product — you'll help decide how cutting-edge models get packaged, governed, and sold to teams and enterprises.

 - High ownership, low process — we value judgment, clarity, and speed over bureaucracy.
   
   


🎯 ABOUT THE ROLE

We're hiring engineers to build the product and infrastructure that lets OpenArt serve teams and enterprises, not just individual creators. That spans the full surface: workspaces and team management, roles and permissions, usage-based billing and procurement-friendly invoicing, audit logs, and the security posture — SSO, data controls, compliance groundwork — that larger customers expect before they'll sign.

This is a full-stack role on a brand-new team. You'll move between customer-facing product (admin consoles, billing UI, workspace settings) and the backend underneath it (access control, usage metering, payment integrations). You'll work closely with the founders and the enterprise team to figure out what "enterprise-ready" means for an AI-native creative platform — and then build it.


🛠 WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Build core enterprise primitives: organizations/workspaces, roles and permissions (RBAC), SSO/SAML, and audit logging

 - Implement usage-based billing, invoicing, and payment flows that support both self-serve and enterprise procurement (e.g. Stripe)

 - Contribute to platform security and reliability work — access control, data isolation, and groundwork for compliance certifications (e.g. SOC 2)

 - Build and maintain backend services and APIs that support multi-tenant, team-based usage patterns

 - Build clean, polished frontend experiences (React/Next.js) for admin, billing, and workspace management

 - Work with founders, sales, and customers to turn real requirements into shipped features

 - Take on increasing ownership as the enterprise platform and team grow




⚙ WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

Core Requirements

 - 2+ years of full-stack engineering experience shipping production software

 - Solid fundamentals in system design and data modeling — you can reason about APIs, permission models, and how data should be structured and isolated

 - Comfortable across the stack: React/Next.js on the front end, Node.js/TypeScript or Python on the back end, and a relational database in between

 - A strong AI-assisted coding practice — you use tools like Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor as a core part of how you build, and have real opinions about what makes them work well

 - Product sense — you care about what makes an admin console feel trustworthy and a workspace feel effortless, not just whether it works

 - Clear communication — you can explain what you built, why, and what the trade-offs were to teammates who aren't engineers




NICE TO HAVE

 - Exposure to payments or billing systems (e.g. Stripe): subscriptions, usage-based billing, invoicing

 - Exposure to auth, security, or compliance work: SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logging, SOC 2 / GDPR

 - Experience with cloud infrastructure (GCP/AWS), observability, or reliability work

 - Startup experience, or having built something 0 to 1 (side projects count)
   
   


💰 COMPENSATION

 - $300k+ total compensation including base salary, bonus, equity

 - Equity - meaningful ownership in what you build

 - High autonomy, high growth environment
   
   


🌍 WORK SETUP

 - Bay Area preferred (hybrid available)

 - Visa sponsorship available
   
   


🎯 WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE IN 3–6 MONTHS

 - You've shipped meaningful pieces of workspaces, permissions, or billing into production, and paying teams are using them

 - You own at least one enterprise surface end to end — e.g. the admin console, audit logs, or invoicing — and are the go-to person for it

 - You've sat in a customer or sales conversation and turned what you heard into a shipped feature

 - You're proposing improvements and catching problems early, not just executing on specs

 - You've grown into more scope than the role started with

If you want to help build the platform that turns a consumer AI product into an enterprise business — and grow fast while doing it — we'd love to talk.
